I want to see if I can afford to buy a car

Two things matter most: the monthly car payment (including insurance and fuel) and how that fits your take-home. Tell me the car price, down payment you’d make, loan term (years) or desired monthly payment, and your monthly take-home so I can check affordability.
Want me to work out your order with your numbers? Four quick questions.
20K, 14% APR, 5 years

A $20,000 car loan at 14% over 5 years costs about $465/month and will pay roughly $7,900 in interest over the life of the loan. Compare that payment plus insurance and fuel to your monthly take-home to judge affordability, and remember 14% is high, if you can, prioritize a lower-rate loan or a larger down payment.
Want me to check that against your pay? Same four quick questions.

Should I pay off my credit card or invest?

Pay off the credit card first if it’s high-interest, that’s a guaranteed return equal to the card’s interest, which beats expected market gains. If the card is low-interest or already paid in full each month, prioritize investing after you keep an emergency fund. Keep it simple: clear high-rate cards, then invest, at least enough to capture any employer match.
